requirement:
A record MUST be changed only if every rewrite a mapping calls for in it
verifies under {cite}`requirements.refactor.outline_inputs`,
{cite}`requirements.refactor.definition_inputs`,
{cite}`requirements.refactor.subject_text`, and
{cite}`requirements.refactor.reference_digest`; otherwise the whole record MUST
be left unchanged and reported with the check that failed. Records that no
mapping affects MUST be left byte-identical.
rationale:
The code mostly implements `requirements.refactor.whole_record`, but it drops the report in one case. A failed `subject_text` or `reference_digest` check is not reported when nothing else about the record changed.

**Obligations and the code that carries them out**
- **Change a record only if every rewrite verifies.**
  - `src/refactor.rs#fn[rewrite_record]` collects failures from each check and returns `Outcome::Unchanged` instead of `Outcome::Changed` if any failed.
  - `outline_inputs` and `definition_inputs` are checked in `src/refactor.rs#fn[rewrite_input]`, which compares the mapped-back hash or definition text with the recorded one. Its `Err` results become `inputs[i]: …` failures.
  - `subject_text` is checked in `rewrite_record`, which compares the mapped-back body (`definitions_back`) with the recorded `requirement` or `example` field.
  - `reference_digest` is checked in `rewrite_record` using `src/refactor.rs#impl[States]/fn[digests]`, which compares the mapped-back digest with the recorded one.
- **Leave the whole record unchanged and report the failed check.** On failure the caller `src/refactor.rs#fn[refactor]` adds the record to the `unchanged` list. It prints the reason in "Left/Would leave N records unchanged" and writes nothing for that record. The rationale is rewritten only on success.
- **Leave unaffected records byte-identical.** `Outcome::Unaffected` records are never written. `refactor` only rewrites records in the `changed` list.

**Tests**
- `tests/refactor.rs#fn[a_moved_function_keeps_its_evidence_current]` covers the success path. It also checks that the unaffected `rules.check` record stays byte-identical.
- `tests/refactor.rs#fn[a_function_edited_while_moving_leaves_its_records_stale]` covers an outline-input failure. The record stays byte-identical and the failure is reported.
- `tests/refactor.rs#fn[a_requirement_edited_while_moving_keeps_its_old_record]` covers a `subject_text` failure.
- `tests/refactor.rs#fn[a_reference_set_changed_beyond_the_mapping_blocks_every_rewrite]` covers a `reference_digest` failure.
- The definition-input failure has a test in `tests/refactor.rs#fn[a_term_edited_while_moving_leaves_its_definition_input_stale]`.

**Gap: a failed check is sometimes not reported**
- In `rewrite_record`, the `subject_text` and `reference_digest` failures are added to `failures` without setting `changed`.
- Only a rename (`new != *name`) or an input outcome sets `changed` afterwards.
- The function returns `Outcome::Unaffected` before it looks at `failures` when `changed` is false.
- So if a mapping calls for a rewrite of the text or digest and the check fails, the failure is lost unless the record is also renamed or an input is touched. Two examples:
  - A reference-set digest affected by a moved file mapping, on a record whose inputs don't read the moved node, with an extra unmapped reference.
  - A body that uses a mapped `{term}` and was edited since it was recorded, on a record whose own requirements input is not flagged.
- The record is left unchanged, but it is not "reported with the check that failed". It is silently classed as unaffected.
- The tests only exercise the cases where a rename or an input failure happens to set `changed`.

Because of this reporting gap, the requirement is not fully satisfied.

selection's current matches are exactly the recorded matches with the mapping

The *mapped-back* form of current text or a current address is the text or
address with each new side of the mappings replaced by its old side.
